message.reasoning_content:
Analyze kernel and record description update. Key risks: packed real FFT via M=N/2 complex FFT of interleaved values; correctness of twiddle table folding, DIF reconstruction, Nyquist bin output. Also note that output FP32 vs tolerance 1e-4. Risks: _twiddle sine at phase>=128? phase values used: (k & (half-1))*(256//width) ranges within [0,256). folded = min(phase,128-phase); phase could exceed 128? twiddle args: in stage, phase max = (half-1)*(256//width) = 256 - 256/width < 128? (half-1)*(256/width): width>=2, half-1 <= width/2-1, phase max = (width/2-1)*(256/width) = 128 - 256/width ≤ 128-... < 128 for width<=128? width max = M ≤128, phase max = 128-256/128? Actually width=M=128: phase max=(63)*(2)=126. Fine. Final twiddle k*(256//N), k up to M-1=N/2-1: phase max = (N/2-1)*(256/N) = 128 - 256/N ≤ 126. OK. But `_twiddle` semantics with folded etc for phases ≤128 works. Cosine table only 65 entries; folded ≤64, |64-phase| ≤64. OK.

DIF: twiddle applied to both halves? In standard DIF, twiddle multiplies the difference part with exponent + (k&mask). Looks plausible. Nyquist bin at k=M: X[Nyquist] = sum (-1)^j x[j] = sum over packed: (ar - ai) at k=0? They store (ar-ai) for k==0 as Nyquist. Hmm need Skeptic. Also note `enable_fp_fusion=False` and float64 compute.

Also key risk: bit-reversal order for DIF then gather address = reverse(k); partner = reverse((-k)&(M-1)). Reconstruction formula sign conventions need checking.

Also LOG_M = m.bit_length()-1; M must be power of two — N in {64,128,256} so M in {32,64,128}, powers of 2. OK.

Also note kernel assumes input row stride = N (contiguous) — validate enforces contiguity, but nonzero storage offsets fine since pointer passed.

Record description update.
